label: T:E
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{T:E}
	Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a Serresubcategory of the category of modules over the 
	Noetherian ring $R$ and let $\mathfrak a=(x_1,\dots,x_s)$ be an ideal of $R$.
	Given an $R$-module $M$ the following conditions are equivalent:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)] $\operatorname{Ext}_R^{i}(R/{\mathfrak a}, M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ 
		for all $i$.
		\item[(ii)] $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(R/{\mathfrak{a}}, M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ for all $i$.
		\item[(iii)] $\operatorname{H}^i(x_1\dots,x_s ; M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ for all $i$.
		\item [(iv)]  $\operatorname{H}_i(x_1,\dots,x_s; M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ for all $i$.
	\end{itemize}
head: environment

label: r:colpow
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{r:colpow}
	Observe that if $\mathcal S$ is a Serre subcategory of the category of $R$-modules
	then for any $R$-module $M$, such that the submodule  $0\underset{M}{:}\mathfrak{a}$ 
	belongs to $\mathcal S$, then for each $l$ also 
	$0\underset{M}{:}\mathfrak{a}^l$  belongs to $\mathcal S$ and if the quotient module
	$M/{{\mathfrak{a}}M}$ belongs to $\mathcal S$, then $M/{{\mathfrak{a}}^lM}$ belong to $\mathcal S$ 
	for all $l$.
	This follows by induction on $l$.
	Let $x_1,\dots,x_s$ be generators of $\mathfrak{a}$. 
	For the first assertion we use the map 
	${0\underset{M}{:}\mathfrak{a}^{l+1}}
	\to{(0\underset{M}{:}\mathfrak{a}^l)_1^s}$, defined by 
	$u\mapsto(x_iu)_1^s$. This map has the kernel $0\underset{M}{:}{\mathfrak{a}}$.
	For the second assertion use the map 
	$(M/{\mathfrak{a}^{l}M})_1^s\to M/{\mathfrak{a}^{l+1}M}$ defined by 
	$({\overline u}_i)_1^s\mapsto{\sum_1^s \overline{x_iu_i}}$, whose cokernel is
	isomorphic to $M/{\mathfrak{a} M}$.

label: T:E
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{T:E}
	Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a Serresubcategory of the category of modules over the 
	Noetherian ring $R$ and let $\mathfrak a=(x_1,\dots,x_s)$ be an ideal of $R$.
	Given an $R$-module $M$ the following conditions are equivalent:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)] $\operatorname{Ext}_R^{i}(R/{\mathfrak a}, M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ 
		for all $i$.
		\item[(ii)] $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(R/{\mathfrak{a}}, M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ for all $i$.
		\item[(iii)] $\operatorname{H}^i(x_1\dots,x_s ; M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ for all $i$.
		\item [(iv)]  $\operatorname{H}_i(x_1,\dots,x_s; M)$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ for all $i$.
	\end{itemize}
head: environment

label: L:I
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:I}
	Let $\mathfrak{a}$ be an ideal of $R$ and let $\mathcal C$ be a class of $R$-modules 
	with the follwing three properties:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(1)] $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal C$.
		\item[(2)] $0\underset{M}{:}\mathfrak{a}\in\mathcal S$ for each $M\in\mathcal C$.
		\item[(3)] If $0\to{M'}\to M\to M^{\prime\prime}\to 0$ is a 
		short exact sequence with $M^{\prime}$ and $M$ in $\mathcal C$, then also 
		$M^{\prime\prime}$ is in $\mathcal C$.
	\end{itemize}
	Let $X^{\bullet}: 0\to X^0\to X^1\to X^2\to\dots$ be a cochain complex 
	such that for every $i$, $X^i\in\mathcal C$ and 
	$\mathfrak{a}\subset\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}\operatorname{H}^i(X^{\bullet})}$. 
	Then  $\operatorname{H}^i(X^{\bullet})\in\mathcal S$ for all $i$.
head: environment

label: L:I_0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:I_0}
	Let $f: M\to N$ be $R$-linear, where both $M$ and $N$ are in $\mathcal C$. 
	Assume that $\mathfrak{a}^l\operatorname{Ker} f=0$ for some $l$.
	Then $\operatorname{Ker} f$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ {\rm(}hence also to $\mathcal C${\rm)} and 
	$\operatorname{Coker} f$ belongs to $\mathcal C$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\operatorname{Ker} f\subset{0\underset{M}{:}\mathfrak{a}^l}$, which belongs to $\mathcal S$ 
	by remark \ref{r:colpow} and the second condition  in 
	Lemma \ref{L:I}. Using the third condition in Lemma \ref{L:I} applied to the 
	exact sequences 
	$0\to\operatorname{Ker} f\to M\to\operatorname{Im} f\to 0$ and 
	$0\to\operatorname{Im} f\to N\to\operatorname{Coker} f\to 0$ 
	we first get that $\operatorname{Im} f\in\mathcal C$ (Note that we assumed that 
	$\mathcal S\subset\mathcal C$) and then that $\operatorname{Coker} f\in\mathcal C$.
head: environment

label: L:I_n
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:I_n}
	Let $ 0\to X^0\overset{d^0}{\to} X^1\to\dots\to X^{n-1}
	\overset{d^{n-1}}{\to} X^n\overset{d^n}{\to} X^{n+1}$
	be  a cocomplex, where each $X^i$ belongs to $\mathcal C$.
	Suppose that there is some $l$, such that $\mathfrak{a}^l\operatorname{H}^i$ are in $\mathcal S$
	for $i=0,\dots,n$. 
	Then the cohomology modules $\operatorname{H}^i$ are in $\mathcal S$ for $i=0,\dots,n$ and 
	$\operatorname{Coker} d^n\in\mathcal C$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use induction on $n$.
	The case $n=0$ follows from Lemma \ref{L:I_0}.
	Let $n>0$ and assume that we have proved the result for $n-1$.
	The map $d^n$ induces a map
	$f : \operatorname{Coker}{d^{n-1}}\to X^{n+1}$. 
	Here both modules belong to $\mathcal C$.
	The first one by the induction hypothesis and 
	the second one by the hypothesis in the lemma. 
	Since $\operatorname{Ker} f=\operatorname{H}^n$ we can apply Lemma \ref{L:I_0} to prove the case 
	$n$.
head: environment

label: L:II
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:II}
	Let $\mathcal C$ be a class of $R$-modules satisfying: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(1)] $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal C$.
		\item[(2)] $M/{\mathfrak{a} M}\in\mathcal S$ for all $M\in\mathcal C$.
		\item[(3)] If $0\to M^{\prime}\to M\to M^{\prime\prime}\to 0$ 
		is a short exact with $M$ and $M^{\prime\prime}$ in $\mathcal C$, 
		then also $M^{\prime}\in\mathcal C$.           
	\end{itemize}
	Let 
	$X_{\bullet}:\dots\to X_2\overset{d_1}{\to} X_1\overset{d_0}{\to} X_0\to 0$ 
	be a chain complex 
	such that for all $i$, $X_i\in\mathcal C$ and 
	$\mathfrak{a}\subset\operatorname{Ann}\sqrt{\operatorname{H}_i(X_{\bullet})}$.
	Then the homology modules 
	$\operatorname{H}_i(X_{\bullet})$ belong to $\mathcal S$  for all $i$.
head: environment

label: L:II_0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:II_0}
	Let $f : M\to N$ be an $R$-linear map, where $M$ and $N$ both are in 
	$\mathcal C$. Assume that ${\mathfrak{a}}^l\operatorname{Coker} f=0$ for some $l$. 
	Then $\operatorname{Ker} f$ and $\operatorname{Coker} f$ belong to $\mathcal C$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\operatorname{Coker} f$ is a homomorhic image of $N/{\mathfrak{a}}^lN$, it follows from 
	(2) in Lemma \ref{L:II} and remark \ref{r:colpow} that 
	$\operatorname{Coker} f\in\mathcal S$ and hence 
	by (1) in Lemma \ref{L:II} that $\operatorname{Coker} f\in\mathcal C$. 
	By property (3) in Lemma \ref{L:II} using the exact sequences 
	$0\to\operatorname{Im} f\to N\to\operatorname{Coker} f\to 0$  and 
	$0\to\operatorname{Ker} f\to M\to\operatorname{Im} f\to 0$ we first get that 
	$\operatorname{Im} f$ belongs to $\mathcal C$ and then that $\operatorname{Ker} f$ belongs to $\mathcal C$.
head: environment

label: L:II_n
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:II_n}
	Let $ X_{n+1}\overset{d_n}{\to} X_n\to\dots
	\to X_1\overset{d_0}{\to} X_0\to 0$ be a  complex. 
	Assume that $X_i\in\mathcal C$ for all $i=0,\dots,n$ and
	that there is $l$, such that ${\mathfrak{a}}^l$ annihilates the homology modules
	$\operatorname{H}_i$ for $i=0,\dots,n$. 
	Then $\operatorname{Ker} d_n$ belongs to  $\mathcal S$ {\rm(}hence also to $\mathcal C${\rm)}  
	and the homology modules 
	$\operatorname{H}_i$ belong to $\mathcal S$ for 
	$i=0,\dots,n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is by induction on $n$.
	The case case $n=0$ is just Lemma \ref{L:II_0}.
	Assume that $n>0$ and that we know that 
	$\operatorname{Ker} d_{n-1}$ belongs to $\mathcal C$ and that the homology modules 
	$\operatorname{H}_i$ belong to
	$\mathcal S$ for $i=0,\dots,n-1$.
	Consider the map $f : X_{n+1}\to \operatorname{Ker} d_{n-1}$ induced by $d_n$. 
	Since $\operatorname{Ker} f=\operatorname{Ker} d_n$ and $\operatorname{Coker} f=\operatorname{H}_{n-1}$ we get by \ref{L:II_0} that 
	$\operatorname{Ker} d_n\in\mathcal C$ and that $\operatorname{H}_{n-1}\in\mathcal S$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have already noticed that the conditions (iii) and (iv) are equivalent.
	Let ${\mathcal C}_i$, ${\mathcal C}_{ii}$, ${\mathcal C}_{iii}$ and ${\mathcal C_{iv}}$ be the classes of 
	modules which satisfy the respective condition in Theorem \ref{T:E}.
	We have already noticed that $\mathcal C_{iii}$ and $\mathcal C_{iv}$ are equal.
	Let $F_{\bullet}\to R/\mathfrak{a}$ be a resolution of $R/\mathfrak{a}$ consisting of 
	finite free modules and let $\operatorname{K}_{\bullet}=\operatorname{K}_\bullet (x_1,\dots,x_s)$ be the 
	Koszul complex  of the sequence $x_1,\dots,x_s$. 
	The classes $\mathcal C_i$ and $\mathcal C_{iii}$ 
	both  satisfy the three  conditions in \ref{L:I}.
	If $M$ is in $\mathcal C_i$ then  by \ref{L:I} the cohomology modules of the
	cochain complex $X^{\bullet}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{K}_{\bullet}, M)$ 
	are in $\mathcal S$ and therefore $M$ is in $\mathcal C_{iii}$.
	Conversely let $M$ be in $\mathcal C_{iii}$. 
	Consider the cochain complex 
	$X^{\bullet}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_{\bullet},M)$. 
	We get using Lemma \ref{L:I}, that $M$   belongs to $\mathcal C_i$. 
	To prove that the classes $\mathcal C_{ii}$ and $\mathcal C_{iv}$ are the same  
	we consider the complexes $\operatorname{K}_{\bullet}\otimes M$ and 
	$F_{\bullet}\otimes M$ and use Lemma~\ref{L:II}.
head: environment

label: T:ET
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal C$ be the class of $R$-modules which satidfy the
	equivalent conditions in Theorem \ref{T:E}. 
	Apply Lemma \ref{L:I} and Lemma \ref{L:II}
	to the complexes $X^{\bullet}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_{\bullet},M)$ and 
	$X_{\bullet}=F_{\bullet}\otimes M$.

label: homext
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{homext} Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of $R$. Let $t\in\Bbb{N}_0$ be an integer and $M$ an $R$-module such that $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/\mathfrak{a},M)$ are finite for all $i\leq t+1$. Let the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^i_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ are ${\rm FD_{<2}}$ ~ $R$-modules for all $i<t$.
	Then, the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^i_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ are $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite for all
	$i<t$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use induction on $t$. The exact sequence 

$$0\longrightarrow \operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M)\longrightarrow M \longrightarrow M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M)
\longrightarrow 0,\,\,\,\,\,\,(*)$$

induces the following exact sequence:

$$0\longrightarrow {\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/\mathfrak{a},\operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M))\longrightarrow{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/\mathfrak{a},M)\longrightarrow {\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/\mathfrak{a},M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M))$$$$\longrightarrow {\operatorname{Ext}}^1_R(R/\mathfrak{a},\operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M))\longrightarrow{\operatorname{Ext}}^1_R(R/\mathfrak{a},M).$$

Since ${\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/\mathfrak{a},M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M))=0$ so ${\rm
	Hom}_R(R/\mathfrak{a},\operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M))$ and ${\rm Ext}^{1}_R(R/\mathfrak{a},\operatorname{\Gamma}_\mathfrak{a}(M))$ are finite. Assume inductively that $t>0$ and that we have established the result for non-negative integers smaller than $t$. Using inductive assumption, the rest of proof is the same as \cite[Theorem 3.4 (i)]{AB}.\qed

label: cof
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cof} Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of $R$. Let $M$ be
	an $R$-module such that the $R$-module  $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/\mathfrak{a} ,M)$ is finite for all $i$ and the $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^i_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ is ${\rm
		FD_{<2}}$ {\rm{(}}or weakly Laskerian{\rm{)}}~ $R$-modules for all $i$. Then the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^i_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ are $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite for all $i$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Follows by Theorem \ref{homext}.\qed
head: manual

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of $R$. Let $M$ be
	an $R$-module such that  the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^i_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ are ${\rm
		FD_{<2}}$ {\rm{(}}or weakly Laskerian{\rm{)}}~ $R$-modules for all $i$. Then, the following conditions are equivalent:
	
	{\rm(i)} The $R$-module  $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/\mathfrak{a} ,M)$ is finite for all $i$.
	
	{\rm(ii)} The $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^i_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ is $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite for all $i$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) Follows by  Corollary \ref{cof}.

(ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) It follows by \cite[Proposition 3.9]{Mel}.\qed

title: Theorem

title: Proof
body_md:
The	case (c) follows by Theorem \cite[Theorem 7.10]{Mel}. 
	
	In the cases (a) and (b), suppose  $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ is $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite for all $i$. It follows from \cite[Corollary 3.10]{Mel} that $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/\mathfrak{a} ,M)$ is a finite $R$-module for all $i$. 
	
	To prove the converse, in the case (b), it follows by \cite[Theorem 2.10]{Mel1}. In the case (a), use \cite[Theorem 3.3]{BA} and the method of proof of \cite[Theorem 2.10]{Mel1}.

label: mar
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{mar}
	
	Let $N$ be a finitely generated $R$-module and $M$ be an arbitrary $R$-module. Let $t$ be a non-negative integer such that ${\operatorname{Ext}}_R^i(N,M)$ is finite for all $0\leq i\leq t$. Then for 
	any finitely generated $R$-module $L$ with
	$\operatorname{Supp}_R(L)\subseteq \operatorname{Supp}_R(N)$, ${\operatorname{Ext}}_R^i(L,M)$ is finite for all integer $0\leq i\leq t$.

label: min
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In order to prove (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii),  use \cite[Theorem 3.3]{BA}, \cite[Theorem 2.3]{Mel1} and \cite[Theorem 7.10]{Mel}, respectively in the cases (a), (b) and (c).
	
	(i)$\Leftrightarrow$(iii) follows by Theorem \ref{cof3}.
	
	(i)$\Leftrightarrow$(iv) follows by Theorem \ref{cof4}.
	
	In order to prove (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(v) and (ii)$\Leftrightarrow$(vii) use  \cite[Lemma 1]{Ka}.
	
	(v)$\Rightarrow$(vi) and (vii)$\Rightarrow$(viii) are trivial.
	
	In order to prove (vi)$\Rightarrow$(v) and (viii)$\Rightarrow$(vii), let $L$ be a finitely generated $R$-module with $\operatorname{Supp}_R(L)\subseteq \operatorname{V}(\mathfrak{a})$. Then $\operatorname{Supp}_R(L)\subseteq \operatorname{Supp}_R(N)$. Now the assertion follows by Lemma \ref{mar}.

label: sez3.11
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{sez3.11}
	Let $\mathfrak{a}$ be an ideals of a Noetherian ring $R$, such that $\dim R/{\mathfrak{a}}=1$. Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module and $r$ an integer. Then $\dim M_{\mathfrak{p}}\leq r$  for each prime ideal  $\mathfrak{p}$ minimal over $\mathfrak{a}$  if and only if $\operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(M))\subseteq \operatorname{Max}(R)$ for all $i>r$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This is the direct consequence of Grothendieck's vanishing theorem and the isomorphism
$\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(M)_{\mathfrak{p}}\cong \operatorname{H}^{i}_{{\mathfrak{a}}R_{\mathfrak{p}}}(M_{\mathfrak{p}})$ for each prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ minimal over $\mathfrak{a}$.
head: environment

label: sez3.12
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The  implications (iii)$\Rightarrow$(ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) always hold, so let us assume (i) and prove that (iii) hold. We do induction on $r$. First we note that if $N$ is a finite $R$-module, such that $\operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(N))\subseteq \operatorname{Max}(R)$, then $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(N)$ is $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite Artinian for all $i$. Let $r=0$ and put $N=M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_{\mathfrak{a}}(M)$. Then $\operatorname{H}^{0}_\mathfrak{a}(N)=0$ and  $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(N)\cong \operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ for all $i>0$.  Hence by the above remark $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(N)$ is $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite Artinian for all $i$. It follows that $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ is Artinian and $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite for all $i>0$. 
	
Next let $r>0$	and put $N=M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_{\mathfrak{a}}(M)$. Then $\operatorname{H}^{0}_\mathfrak{a}(N)=0$ and we can take $x\in \mathfrak{a}$ such that $x$ is $N$-regular.

Then by Lemma \ref{sez3.11}, $\dim(N/xN)_{\mathfrak{p}}\leq r-1$ for each prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ minimal over $\mathfrak{a}$. Applying the induction hypothesis to $N/xN$, we have that $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(N/xN)$ is $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite Artinian for all $i>r-1$. Next applying local cohomology functor to the exact sequence $0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow N \longrightarrow N/xN
	\longrightarrow 0,$ we can conclude that $(0:_{\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(N)}x)$ is $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite Artinian for all $i>r$. It follows that $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(N)$ is Artinian and $\mathfrak{a}$-cofinite for all $i>r$. Therefore also $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\mathfrak{a}(M)$ , for all $i>r$.
